### Issues
**[CR-R10-1][MEDIUM][statement-contradiction][HIGH]** rows 6/15 order P where no writable carrier exists
File: r10:60, :62 vs :72 C4b(iv), :16 R6, :95 AC6(d), :154
R9-3 makes a non-object upstream SC a carrier failure with “nothing replaced … M/L+C”, and R6/AC6(d) scope P to “where a carrier exists”, yet rows 6/15 keep unqualified “P + L + C”; the override column covers only reserved-key collisions, impossible on a non-object SC. The normative table orders a write an array/string cannot carry, contradicting C4b(iv) and the R9-3 oracle. Adjacent: row 9’s “—” shape leaves select-present + non-object SC without reason precedence.
Fix: “P only where a writable SC carrier exists (multiplexer envelope or direct object SC); direct non-object SC ⇒ M-when-rendered else L+C”; pin select-present vs carrier-failure precedence.

**[CR-R10-2][MEDIUM][statement-contradiction][HIGH]** AC4 asserts the direct-path override on both paths
File: r10:93 vs :51 row 5, :48 R2, :89 AC1
AC4 requires the matching-forged oracle “(both paths)” and a decision that “follows the override (skip…)”. The override/`mcp_bridge_projection` is direct-only (C3:69, C4b:72, R6:16); on the multiplexer a nested forged member is a non-payload member preserved value-identically and row 5 decides APPLY with a legitimate applied:true envelope disclosure — falsifying both “skip” and “no bridge-attached applied:true member exists anywhere”.
Fix: scope the clause and “(both paths)” to the direct path (AC1:89 does), or state the multiplexer expectation (row 5 APPLY; nested member inert).

**[CR-R10-3][LOW][repair-completeness][HIGH]** T2’s R9-2 reword is absent
File: r10:107 == r9:106; r10:32, :153
“pass-through preserving original bytes” survives although §10:153 claims T2 reworded; E19:32 rules upstream-byte preservation unachievable, and raw-byte embedding would break AC4’s byte-identity-to-today (:93).
Fix: “pass-through leaves the `upstream_result` value unchanged (decoded-value identity); do not embed raw upstream bytes”.

**[CR-R10-4][LOW][editorial][MEDIUM]** override L/C reads as an alternative
File: r10:50, rows 5/6/13/14/17, :68 vs :65 “M + L + C”, :89, :95
“channel becomes M … when rendered, else L+C” can be read as dropping the warn record and counter when rendered; AC1 and AC6(d) require one of each always. Fix: state once that override rows always emit L+C, plus M when rendered within budget.

**[CR-R10-5][LOW][spec-gap][MEDIUM]** unreachable override rows
File: r10:37, :53, :102
The override lists rows 15/17 (fields-mode), but fields cannot be requested on the direct path (R3:13), so the demanded oracles cannot be built end-to-end. Fix: drop 15/17 or mark engine-synthetic only.
